info.title: NomaUBL API
info.description:
REST API of the NomaUBL e-invoicing platform: invoices from JD Edwards or any source turned into UBL 2.1, validated, submitted to a French Plateforme Agréée (PA), tracked through their lifecycle, plus e-reporting, the e-directory, the configuration and the operations of the instance.

## Getting started

**Session.** `POST /api/auth/login` with a username and password returns a bearer token; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other call. `GET /api/auth/session` tells whether a token is still valid. With authentication disabled on the instance, every call is accepted without a token. The public routes (login, session, password reset, single sign-on, license, build info, branding, the inbound webhook) carry `security: []` in this document.

**Rights.** An operation that needs a grant carries `x-permission`: an action name the user's role must allow (for example `invoice.resend`, `integration-run`), or `settings (feature)` for the configuration screens. A read-only role is refused every action. Row filters of the role (companies, document types) apply to the lists.

**Responses.** JSON. Success is `{ "success": true, … }`; a failure is `{ "success": false, "error": "message" }` with the HTTP status (400 bad input, 401 no session, 403 refused, 404 not found, 405 wrong method, 500 server error). Files come back with their own content type.

**Invoice key.** An invoice is identified by the JD Edwards triplet `doc` (document number), `dct` (document type) and `kco` (company), in the path as `/{doc}/{dct}/{kco}`. The UBL invoice number is their concatenation.

**Dates.** Query parameters take ISO dates `yyyy-MM-dd`; stored dates are JD Edwards Julian integers (CYYDDD, e.g. 126292 = 2026-10-19) and are returned converted to ISO by the list endpoints.

**Lists and paging.** List endpoints take `page` and `pageSize` and return `{ total, items }` (the field name is given per endpoint); filters are query parameters named after the columns of the list view.

**Background runs.** A long operation (status integrity, ordering check, e-reporting generation, watched-folder scan, bulk reprocess) returns at once `{ "success": true, "running": true }`; poll the matching `GET …/progress` (or the same path with GET) until `running` is false: the response then carries the result and `logs`, an array of `{ severity, module, submodule, message }` lines. Starting a run that is already running returns `running: true` again, nothing is launched twice.

**Streaming.** `POST /api/ai/chat` answers with Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`), one `data:` JSON object per event: `token` (text), `tool_call` (name, summary), `error`.

**Behind a proxy.** The server URL of this document follows the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header, so Try it out targets the right path under a reverse proxy.

**Versioning.** The document is generated by the running server; its version is the release of the jar.

post.description:
Authenticates a user with username and password and returns a Bearer token.

The token must be included in the Authorization header for all subsequent API calls. Returns the token along with the full user profile (username, role, fullName, email). This is the only endpoint (along with /api/auth/session) that does not require prior authentication.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

Invalidates the current Bearer token, ending the user session.

The token is extracted from the Authorization header. After logout, the token can no longer be used for API calls. Returns success even if the token was already expired or invalid.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Validates the current Bearer token and returns the authenticated user profile.

Also returns whether authentication is enabled on this server instance (authEnabled flag). If the token is missing or invalid, user is null but the call still succeeds — this allows the frontend to detect whether login is required. This endpoint does not require prior authentication.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

post.description:
Changes the password for the currently authenticated user.

Requires the current (old) password for verification and the new password. The new password must be at least 4 characters long. The user is identified from the session token in the Authorization header.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Starts the self-service password reset.

Both username and email are required and must match the same active account. Always returns a generic success regardless of whether the pair matches, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts. When SMTP is configured and the pair matches, a one-shot reset token (60-minute TTL) is generated and the reset URL is emailed to the user. The link base comes from the global template's publicBaseUrl, falling back to the request's Origin header. This endpoint is public — no Bearer token required.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

post.summary: Consume a reset token and set a new password
post.description:
Completes the password reset started by /api/auth/forgot-password.

The token is the one-shot UUID from the emailed reset link and expires after 60 minutes. The new password must be at least 4 characters long. Returns an error for an invalid or expired token. This endpoint is public — no Bearer token required.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

get.description:
Builds the identity provider's authorization URL from the configured OIDC template and returns it; the browser is expected to navigate to redirectUrl.

PKCE verifier and nonce are stashed server-side under a random state value the IdP echoes back on the callback. returnTo preserves the in-app path the user was trying to reach so the callback can land there after login. Returns an error when OIDC is not enabled or the template is incomplete. Public endpoint.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

parameters.name: returnTo
parameters.description: In-app path to redirect to after successful login

get.description:
The identity provider redirects the browser here after authentication.

The server exchanges the authorization code for tokens, verifies the ID token, looks up or provisions the matching user, and mints a NomaUBL session. The response is an HTML page (not JSON) that stores the session token in localStorage and redirects into the SPA at the preserved returnTo path. On error (IdP error, missing email claim, refused domain) an HTML error page is returned instead. Public endpoint.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Authorization code issued by the IdP

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque state value echoed back by the IdP

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: IdP error code when the handshake failed

schema.example: text/html page that stores the session token and redirects into the SPA

get.description:
Returns the list of all registered users with their profiles (username, role, fullName, email, active status).

Passwords are never included in the response. Requires authentication. Typically restricted to admin users in the frontend.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Creates a new user account with the specified username, password, role, and optional profile fields.

The username must be unique. If no role is specified, defaults to 'viewer'. forcePasswordChange (default true) asks for a new password at the first local login; a blank password creates an SSO-only account with no local password, which cannot log in locally and is never asked to change a password. Requires authentication. The password is stored hashed.

**Access:** settings (feature).

put.description:
Updates an existing user's role, fullName, email, active status, and optionally resets their password (forcePasswordChange, default true, asks for a new one at the next local login).

The username is specified in the URL path. If newPassword is provided, the user's password is changed without requiring the old password (admin reset). Requires authentication.

**Access:** settings (feature).

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a user account.

The username is specified in the URL path. Active sessions for the deleted user are not automatically invalidated. Requires authentication.

**Access:** settings (feature).

get.description:
Returns the list of all defined roles with their permissions.

Each role includes a name, description, allowed pages (comma-separated), allowed companies, and a settings flag indicating whether the role can access configuration. Requires authentication.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Creates a new role with the specified permissions.

The name must be unique. The pages field is a comma-separated list of allowed page identifiers (or '*' for all pages). The companies field restricts which company codes (UHKCO) the role can access. The settings flag controls access to the configuration management UI. Requires authentication.

**Access:** settings (feature).

put.description:
Updates an existing role's description, pages, companies, and settings flag.

The role name is specified in the URL path and cannot be changed. Changes take effect on the next page load for users with this role. Requires authentication.

**Access:** settings (feature).

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a role definition.

Users currently assigned to this role will retain their role name but may lose access to restricted pages. The role name is specified in the URL path. Requires authentication.

**Access:** settings (feature).

post.description:
Creates the authentication tables (users, roles, sessions) if they do not exist, and bootstraps a default admin user (admin/admin) if no users are found.

This endpoint is idempotent — calling it multiple times is safe. After initialization, the server reloads the auth configuration. Use this when setting up a new NomaUBL instance or after a database migration.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

get.description:
Returns the list of all templates defined in config.json, including system templates (global, e-invoicing, e-directory) and document templates (e.g. invoices, credit_notes).

Each template includes its name, description, type, and all key-value properties. Use this to populate template selectors in the UI.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Returns a single template including all its properties. The template name is passed as a query parameter. Returns an error if the template does not exist.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Creates a new configuration template.

The template name must be unique. System template names (global, e-invoicing, e-directory) cannot be used for new templates. The template is persisted to config.json immediately.

**Access:** settings (feature).

put.description:
Replaces all properties of an existing template with the provided values.

The template name is specified as a query parameter. If the template is e-invoicing, the server reloads PA API credentials after saving.

**Access:** settings (feature).

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a template from config.json.

System templates (global, e-invoicing, e-directory) cannot be deleted and will return an error. Document templates can be deleted freely.

**Access:** settings (feature).

post.description:
Duplicates an existing template under a new name.

Both the source (from) and destination (to) names are required. The destination name must not already exist. All properties from the source template are copied to the new template.

**Access:** settings (feature).

Single processing entry point.

The pipeline is selected by the document template's `source` property: XML (XML spool input → XSL transform → UBL), UBL (already-formed UBL invoice; (doc, dct, kco) parsed from cbc:ID via the template's `idPattern` regex), connector, or PDF (text PDF converted to a flat XML of labelled values, one table and raw rows — settings pdf.tableStart / pdf.tableEnd / pdf.match / pdf.pageMatch / pdf.field.N — then processed as XML). When replaceMode is true, existing invoices in the database are overwritten. XML-source flags: noSend (skip PA send), mode (AUTO|SINGLE|BURST|UBL). UBL-source flags: validateOnly (no DB / no PA), sendToPA (Y|N — overrides settings). repairMode (all sources): rebuilds the invoice tables (header, lines, VAT, validation) of a document whose F564230 archive and F564235 history survived a lost replace — archive and history untouched, no lifecycle event written, header status/reason/action copied from the latest history event, never sent to the PA. Implies replace; ignores noSend/sendToPA/validateOnly.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Convert a text PDF to the flat XML of a PDF-source template
post.description:
Body: raw PDF bytes (application/octet-stream).

Query: template (optional — its pdf.tableStart / pdf.tableEnd / pdf.match / pdf.field.N settings; defaults otherwise), filename. Returns the XML text the PDF-source pipeline would process: one element per labelled value, <Lignes>/<Ligne> for the table, <Textes>/<Texte> for every row. Preview only: nothing is written to dirInput. Used by the document editor and the XSL editor to load a sample straight from a PDF.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Validates a UBL XML file against XSD and Schematron rules.

For sourceType=xml: generates UBL from raw source XML first (no DB write, no PA send), then validates. For sourceType=ubl: validates the UBL file directly. Returns structured validation results.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Runs a document template's spool-enrichment rules against a sample source spool WITHOUT touching the database or the normal pipeline — used by the Enrichment editor's Dry-run button.

The request body is a FLAT JSON object of the (possibly unsaved) enrich.* rule properties plus _xml (the sample spool). Each rule fetches data from a SQL / API connector and injects it into the spool before transformation; the LIVE connectors are called. Returns the enriched XML, a one-line summary (rules / matched nodes / fields added / connector calls) and any warnings. On a blocking rule failure or bad input, returns { success: false, error }.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Builds the canonical invoice XML for a connector-source document template WITHOUT running the full UBL pipeline — the XSL Editor's 'Load connector sample' button uses it to feed the XPath designer view.

The template must have source=connector; params are passed through to the connector calls and the LIVE connectors are called. Returns the serialised XML plus any non-blocking warnings.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Fetch received (inbound) invoices from the PA
post.description:
Runs the received-invoice handler synchronously: pulls inbound supplier invoices from the Plateforme Agreee and records them locally.

Console output from the run is captured and returned as structured log entries, the same shape as the other processing endpoints. Requires the integration-run action grant when roles are enforced.

**Access:** integration-run.

Queries all invoices currently in status 9906 (pending) and checks their import status on the Plateforme Agreee.

For each invoice, calls GET /api/v1/sale/invoices/import/{uuid}. Updates the database accordingly: success -> status 10 (Deposited) with invoiceUuid, failed -> status 9907 with error messages, pending -> no change. This is typically called periodically or on-demand after invoice submission.

**Access:** integration-run.

Retrieves updated lifecycle statuses from the PA API for all submitted invoices.

This fetches the latest status transitions (e.g. received, under processing, approved, rejected) and records them in the lifecycle table (F564235). Use this to keep the local database in sync with the PA's invoice status.

**Access:** integration-run.

get.description:
Progress endpoint for the background run started by POST /api/import.

Returns the run's structured log entries captured so far plus a running flag the UI polls until it turns false. Safe to call at any time — when no run is active it returns the last run's logs.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Progress endpoint for the background run started by POST /api/retrieve-statuses.

Returns the structured log entries captured so far plus a running flag the UI polls until it turns false.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Returns {running:true} plus the log lines emitted so far (logs[]: fetch pages, compare progress) while the background integrity check started by the POST is still working, then the stored result with the full log: totals (totalEvents, alreadyRecorded, missing, applied, invoiceNotFound, unmappedCode, superseded) plus a per-event details array.

Returns an error when no integrity run has been started yet in this server session.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Starts a background check that fetches every PA event since the given date and compares it with the recorded lifecycle: a dry run (apply=false) reports the missing events, apply=true backfills them (idempotent — already-recorded codes are no-ops). fireNotifications controls whether backfilled transitions also fire notification rules; keys optionally restricts the run to specific event keys. until (optional, default now) bounds the PA search window on the right — exposed to the connector as {{toDate}} / {{toDateRaw}}; company (optional kco) limits the fetch to that company's status connector and the invoice lookup to that company.

Plain dates are widened to the full day. The regular poll's watermark is never touched. Returns {running:true} immediately — poll the GET for the result. Requires the integration-run action grant.

**Access:** integration-run.

DB-only scan for PA-stage internal (99xx) lifecycle rows recorded AFTER a standard cycle-de-vie status (state misordered / invalid), standard statuses out of order (out-of-order, repaired by re-sequencing) and invoice headers that differ from the latest real state of their history (header-drift, key doc|dct|kco|header; the history-only markers 9912 and 9908 are looked past).

A dry run (apply=false) reports the findings; apply=true deletes / re-sequences the selected rows and realigns the invoice header with the last real state. keys optionally restricts the fix. Runs in the background (whole-table scan): the POST returns {running:true}; poll GET on the same path for the log lines so far, then the result with the full log. Runs synchronously and returns the same result shape as the integrity check. Requires the integration-run action grant.

**Access:** integration-run.

post.summary: Receive a PA status webhook (inbound push)
post.description:
Public endpoint the Plateforme Agreee calls to push a document status update — the push counterpart of the /api/import poll.

It bypasses the session Bearer guard; instead the call is authenticated by an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the request, verified against the connector's shared secret (webhook.secret). `{connector}` is the api-connector template name that carries the webhook config; `{event}` selects the handler (currently `status`). The receiver extracts the PA transaction id and status from the JSON body using the connector's configurable JSON paths (webhook.idField, webhook.statusField, webhook.eventIdField), resolves the id to the invoice via F564230.FEUKIDSZ, translates the status through webhook.statusMap (paStatus:logical pairs, logical in success|pending|failed) and applies the matching transition (success -> Deposited, pending -> 9906, failed -> 9907), writing F564231 + F564235. Duplicate deliveries are deduped by the event id. Per the spec it always returns 2xx within 60s on a valid signature — even when the payload can't be matched — and returns 401 only when the signature check fails.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

parameters.name: connector
parameters.description: api-connector template name carrying the webhook config

parameters.name: X-Signature
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA256 signature of the canonical request, verified against webhook.secret

parameters.name: X-Timestamp
parameters.description: Request timestamp folded into the signed canonical string

parameters.name: X-Checksum
parameters.description: Optional SHA-256 of the body, compared before the signature check

post.description:
Pauses or resumes one background job without restarting the server: job is any job id of the status payload (import, status, ereporting, received, notificationsRetention, fetchAll.<label>, digest.<name>, retry.<name>, statusCheck.<name>).

A paused job keeps its schedule but its fires are skipped; Run now ignores the pause. Runtime-only — a server restart always resumes every job, so a pause can never be forgotten forever. Complementary: the global fetchQuietFrom / fetchQuietTo properties (HH:mm, may cross midnight) define a daily window during which both pollers skip their runs automatically — set it over the send campaigns so per-invoice import polls don't pile up on the PA (requested by @GP). Returns the fresh scheduler status.

**Access:** integration-run.

Runs the retention purge in dry-run mode with the days saved in the global settings: counts the rows each store would lose (processing rows, step timings, job runs, validation errors of finished invoices, notifications) and deletes nothing.

Same as nomaubl.sh purge --dry-run.

**Access:** integration-run.

get.description:
Returns the last runs of one background job, newest first, from the job run rows the scheduler writes to the runtime processing log (mode JOB): one START row when the job begins and one END or ERROR row when it finishes, with the duration and a one-line summary.

Survives server restarts, unlike the in-memory stats of the status endpoint. job is the job id of the status payload; limit defaults to 20.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Re-reads the configuration and re-arms every background job (polls, batch jobs, digests, auto-retries, lifecycle checks, retention) without restarting the server.

Called by the Scheduled jobs page after a save so the new trigger is live at once. Operator pause switches are kept; a run in progress completes. Returns the fresh scheduler status.

**Access:** integration-run.

Fires one background job immediately on the scheduler's executor, outside its cadence, ignoring the pause switch and the quiet window.

The run is recorded like a scheduled fire, so the Scheduled jobs page shows its outcome. job is the job id of the status payload: import, status, ereporting, received, notificationsRetention, fetchAll.<label>, digest.<name>, retry.<name>, statusCheck.<name>. A job already running is not started twice.

**Access:** integration-run.

get.description:
Returns the current background scheduler configuration and status.

The scheduler runs periodic tasks in serve mode: import-status polling, PA status retrieval, and batch document processing. Intervals are configured via global template properties: fetchImportInterval, fetchStatusInterval, fetchAllInterval (minutes, 0=disabled). fetchAllParams holds a JSON string with the same fields as BatchRunRequest.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Two request forms. {"identifier":"..."} probes one addressing identifier's reachability on the PPF (the same non-blocking check the processing pipeline runs before a send) and returns {found, message}. {"siren":"..."} lists every routing line registered in the PPF directory for the SIREN through the connector's directory-check-siren endpoint — identifiers may be SIREN, SIREN_SIRET, SIREN_SIRET_ROUTING or SIREN_SUFFIX — and returns {success, configured, lines:[{identifier, siret, suffix, routingIdentifier, platform, status, name}]}; platform is null when the PA response carries no reachability flag, and configured=false means the connector defines no listing endpoint (the E-Directory page shows a notice). Uses the connector referenced by the e-directory configuration template.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of invoices from the invoice header table with optional filtering and sorting.

Supports full-text search across document number, type, and company code, as well as filters by status code, UBL invoice number, customer reference/name, and issue date range. Results include invoice metadata, amounts, customer info, and current status.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Full-text search on DOC, DCT, KCO fields

parameters.name: customer
parameters.description: Filter by customer reference or name

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Column to sort by (e.g. fedoc, issueDate, statusCode)

parameters.name: sortDir
parameters.description: Sort direction: ASC or DESC (default DESC)

parameters.name: excludeReviewedErrors
parameters.description: true = drop reviewed invoices (UHALRTPSD = Y) that sit in an errorTech / errorBusiness status — the dashboard / reports drill-down filter. Default false.

post.summary: Create an invoice from form fields
post.description:
Creates a new invoice header row from flat form fields — the manual-entry path used by the Create dialog, as opposed to /api/invoices/create-ubl which parses a full UBL document. doc, dct and kco are mandatory and become the primary key; the remaining fields (ublNumber, issueDate, invoiceType, amounts, customer info) are optional.

Requires the invoice-create action grant when roles are enforced.

**Access:** invoice.create.

put.description:
Updates the editable header fields (ublNumber, issueDate, invoiceType, amounts, customer info) on an existing invoice row.

The key columns cannot be changed. Requires the invoice-edit action grant; invoices outside the caller's company / row grants are reported as not found so existence is not leaked.

**Access:** invoice.edit.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes the invoice header plus its dependent rows (lifecycle events, validation errors, lines, VAT) and the F564230 log row (source XML, PA transaction UUID, source file name) in a single transaction.

Refused on PA-protected statuses (any standard lifecycle code, 9911, 9913), except a 213 Rejetée for an addressing reason (ADR_ERR, REJ_ADR, DEST_INC) — same rule as the edit window and Fix buyer. Requires the invoice-delete action grant; invoices outside the caller's company / row grants are reported as not found.

**Access:** invoice.delete.

get.description:
Counts invoices held for review — status 9900/9901/9902 whose archive-log row carries the send-to-PA flag value 3 (waiting).

Drives the 'waiting' badge on the invoice list and the bulk 'send all waiting' action.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Returns aggregated counts of invoices grouped by status code for dashboard display.

Each entry includes the status code, human-readable label, and count. Optionally filtered by last update date range. Use this to populate status chips or a summary dashboard.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: excludeReviewed
parameters.description: true = drop reviewed invoices (UHALRTPSD = Y) that sit in an errorTech / errorBusiness status; other statuses keep them. Default false.

get.description:
Returns all lifecycle events from the lifecycle table (F564235) for the given invoice.

Events are ordered by sequence number and include status code, label, message, and timestamp. The invoice is identified by its primary key: doc (UHDOC), dct (UHDCT), kco (UHKCO).

**Access:** any signed-in user.

delete.description:
Removes a single status event (F564235 row, identified by its sequence number) from the invoice's history, then realigns the header status (F564231) with the last remaining event.

Manual cleanup for stray PA events — e.g. a Refusée delivered although the PA later kept processing the invoice. Requires the dedicated invoice.lifecycle-delete action. Nothing else is touched; the operation is one event at a time by design.

**Access:** invoice.lifecycle-delete.

get.description:
Returns validation errors from the validation table (F564236) for the given invoice.

Errors include severity level (FATAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO), validation source (XSD or Schematron), rule identifier, and a human-readable error message. Only present for invoices that failed or passed with warnings.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Returns the line items extracted from the UBL XML document for the given invoice.

Each line includes item description, quantity, unit price, line amount, VAT category and rate. The UBL XML is retrieved from the BLOB column in the invoice header table.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Returns the VAT breakdown rows from the UBL XML document's TaxTotal section.

Each row includes the tax category, rate, taxable base amount, VAT amount, currency, and exemption reason (if applicable). Useful for displaying a VAT summary table in the invoice detail view.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Parses cbc:Note elements from the UBL XML stored in F564231.UHTXFT.

Notes with a #PREFIX# marker (e.g. #PMD#text) are split into prefix and text fields. Returns notes as [{prefix, text}, ...] objects.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Returns the invoice header's CURRENT status context from F564231: reason code and label, expected-action code, label and note, plus the full status message.

Shown under the status badge in the invoice modal and merged into the custom-action placeholder context so {reasonLabel} / {actionLabel} / {actionNote} resolve without adding the columns to the list view. Returns {success:false} when the invoice is unknown or not visible to the caller.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

example.statusMsg: Deposited but not transmitted to the recipient platform

get.description:
Returns the raw UBL 2.1 XML stored in F564231.UHTXFT as a JSON string.

The invoice detail modal uses it to render Parties, Invoice Lines, VAT recap and Notes client-side. An invoice that is missing or not visible to the caller returns the same 'not found' error, so existence is not leaked.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Runs the archived UBL through the post-transform stylesheet of the invoice's document template (postTransform / postTransformSuffix, e.g. the shipped ubl-to-cii.xsl) and returns the result as a JSON string with the file name to save it under and the template's name for it (postTransformName, e.g.

CII). Computed on demand, nothing is stored. Error when the template names no post-transform; same visibility rule as /xml.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Creates a new invoice by parsing a UBL 2.1 XML document and inserting header, lines, VAT summary, and lifecycle event into the database using UBLDatabaseHandler.

The XML must conform to EN 16931 UBL 2.1 structure with proper namespaces. alertProcessed="Y" also marks the invoice as reviewed by customer service (F564231.UHALRTPSD) when the validation raises no error — what the invoice window sends; default N.

**Access:** invoice.create.

Re-submits the invoice's UBL XML to the Plateforme Agreee.

The XML is retrieved from the database BLOB and sent via the PA import API. A new UUID is assigned and the invoice status is updated to 9906 (pending). Use this when a previous submission failed or was rejected and the issue has been resolved. The connector body receives the same placeholders as the initial send, including {{derivedContent}} / {{derivedFilePath}} (the document template's post-transform output, computed again from the archived UBL; empty when the template has none).

**Access:** invoice.resend.

post.summary: Fix buyer identifiers in the stored UBL
post.description:
Surgically corrects the buyer identifiers inside the stored UBL (F564231 BLOB) — the most frequent PA rejection causes: SIREN (BT-47), SIRET (BT-46), intra-community VAT (BT-48) and electronic address (BT-49).

Only the fields present in the body change; the rest of the document stays byte-identical. The endpoint scheme is endpointScheme when given, else the scheme already on the document, else 0225 (French PPF routing scheme); an empty siret removes the optional BT-46. The patched document is then revalidated and stored through the same pipeline as the edit window (status 9901/9902/9905, F564236 refreshed, audit lifecycle event with old/new values). Refused on PA-protected statuses, except a 213 Rejetée whose reason is an addressing one (ADR_ERR, REJ_ADR, DEST_INC): the invoice never reached the customer, so it may be repaired and resent. alertProcessed="Y" also marks the invoice as reviewed by customer service (F564231.UHALRTPSD) when the validation raises no error; default N. resend=true chains a resend when the invoice is sendable after revalidation.

**Access:** invoice.edit.

Manually sets the invoice status either via the PA API (target=pa, which calls the PA's status update endpoint) or directly in the local database (target=db, which updates F564231 and inserts a lifecycle event in F564235).

Use target=db for corrections or when the PA is unreachable. The status code and name follow the UNTDID 1373 standard or internal 99xx codes.

**Access:** invoice.status.pa (platform statuses) or invoice.status.db (local statuses).

post.x-permission: any signed-in user; the document template must allow it (allowReprocess for a reprint, allowFullReprocess for a 9905)
post.summary: Reprocess one invoice from archived source
post.description:
Reprints the invoice: regenerates its outputs (readable PDF/XML plus the UBL file) from the archived JDE source spool (F564230.FETXFT) into the output folders WITHOUT any database change, WITHOUT re-validating the UBL and WITHOUT sending to the PA — the stored e-invoice and its validation results stay as they are, the status/reason/message are kept and a single 9912 'Retraitement' lifecycle event is appended, which also makes the invoice ineligible for a second reprocess.

The kind follows the status: a validation-failed invoice (9905) on a template with allowFullReprocess=Y is reprocessed in full, a Deposited NON_TRANSMISE one on a template with allowReprocess=Y is reprinted; kind=reprint|full in the body forces one. In the full kind the archived source goes through the normal pipeline again as a history-preserving replace: enrichment re-queried, UBL regenerated, validated and sent when the template and document type say so; the 9912 marker is written first and opens a new submission cycle, and a full reprocess may run again later. The template is read from the invoice row, never chosen by the caller.

**Access:** any signed-in user; the document template must allow it (allowReprocess for a reprint, allowFullReprocess for a 9905).

Kicks off a background bulk-resend over the supplied selection and returns the new job id immediately; the UI polls GET /api/jobs/{id} for progress. keys ([{doc,dct,kco}, ...]) wins over the status / date-range filter when present; the default status filter is 9904 (send failed). delayMs throttles between sends and parallel sets the worker count — both default from the global settings (bulkSendDelayMs / bulkSendParallel) and are capped server-side. sendToPaFlag optionally restricts to a FEEV10 value (e.g. 3 = send all waiting).

Requires the invoice-resend action grant.

**Access:** invoice.resend.

post.x-permission: any signed-in user; the document template must allow it (allowReprocess / allowFullReprocess)
post.description:
Reprocesses the supplied key list synchronously with the same flow as the single reprocess endpoint — the kind follows each invoice's status (9905 → full, 200 NON_TRANSMISE → reprint), kind=reprint|full forces one.

The invoices are staged and processed as ONE batch per template and kind, in the background: the POST returns {running:true}; poll GET /api/invoices/reprocess-all for the log, then the ok/failed tally plus a compact per-key result list.

**Access:** any signed-in user; the document template must allow it (allowReprocess / allowFullReprocess).

post.x-permission: any signed-in user; the document template must allow it (allowReprocess / allowFullReprocess)
post.description:
Runs in the background as one staged batch per template (POST returns {running:true}; GET on the same path polls the log, then the tally).

With {"kind":"full"}: every validation-failed (9905) invoice on a template with allowFullReprocess=Y, reprocessed in full. Default: reprints EVERY eligible invoice — Deposited (200) with reason NON_TRANSMISE, not already reprocessed (no 9912 event) and whose template opts in — rather than a hand-picked selection. Same synchronous, history-preserving, no-send flow per invoice; also the entry point for the -reprocess CLI mode. Returns the same ok/failed tally as the bulk endpoint.

**Access:** any signed-in user; the document template must allow it (allowReprocess / allowFullReprocess).

get.summary: Count reprocess-eligible invoices (kind=full for the validation-failed set)
get.description:
Returns how many invoices are currently eligible for reprocess (Deposited 200 with reason NON_TRANSMISE, no prior 9912 event, template opted in).

Drives the Tech Dashboard 'Reprocess' card so its total matches what reprocess-all would actually run.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Validates the UBL XML stored in the database (F564231.UHTXFT) for the given invoice against XSD schema and Schematron business rules.

Returns a status field: 'valid' (no issues), 'warning' (warnings only), or 'error' (has errors). The errors array contains detailed validation results with severity, source, rule, and message.

**Access:** invoice.validate.

get.description:
Generates a PDF from the UBL XML stored in the database and appends any embedded PDF attachment.

The invoice can be identified in two ways: (1) by the UBL invoice number via the id query parameter (matched against UHK74FLEN), or (2) by the (doc, dct, kco) composite key via the doc, dct and kco query parameters. When all three of doc/dct/kco are present they take precedence over id. The lang parameter controls the language of labels in the generated PDF (fr or en). Reference list labels (invoice types, payment means) are resolved from configuration. This endpoint is designed to be opened directly in a browser tab or iframe.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UBL invoice number (UHK74FLEN). Required when doc/dct/kco are not all provided.

parameters.name: doc
parameters.description: Document number (UHDOC). Use together with dct and kco for an unambiguous lookup.

parameters.name: dct
parameters.description: Document type (UHDCT). Use together with doc and kco.

parameters.name: kco
parameters.description: Company code (UHKCO). Use together with doc and dct.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Language code for PDF labels: 'fr' or 'en' (default: en)

post.description:
Lists all XML files in the input directory.

The directory is selected by the document template's `source` property: XML → dirInput with %TEMPLATE% resolved; UBL → dirInput/ubl.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: List BIP jobs for batch processing
post.description:
Queries the JDE BIP Print Queue for jobs newer than the specified lastJobNumber (or the lastBipJobNumber from the global config if not provided).

Only returns jobs matching the report filters defined in the configuration. Each entry includes the job number and base file name. Use this to discover new print jobs that are ready for UBL processing.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Max BIP job number per host
post.description:
Returns MAX(RJJOBNBR) for every JDE execution host found in the BIP Print Queue.

Job numbers are unique per host, so the settings UI uses this to seed the per-host watermarks (lastBipJobNumber.<host>) one time before enabling the batch fetch loop.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Processes multiple files in batch mode.

The pipeline is selected by the document template's `source` property (XML → -process subprocess; UBL → in-process via UBLInvoiceProcessor with cbc:ID regex parsing). Source 'directory' scans dirInput (XML) or dirInput/ubl (UBL). Source 'bip' extracts from BIP Print Queue jobs. Duplicate documents are skipped when replaceMode is false.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Runs the watched-folder pickup (watch-folders template): lists each folder for files matching its name pattern and newer than its watermark minus the overlap, drops the ones already in F564230 (source file name) or already waiting as XML in the input folder, converts the PDFs in parallel into the document template's input folder, then runs one -process batch per template. folder limits the run to one entry (1-based), since widens the window for a backfill (yyyy-MM-dd or ISO instant), dryRun only reports, noProcess converts without the batch.

The watermark advances to the scan start on every non-dry run. Runs in the background: the POST returns {running:true}; poll GET on the same path for the log lines so far, then the result with the full log. A template whose input folder is locked by a running batch is not started again (batches[template] says SKIPPED).

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Applies post-generation processing to a BIP Print Queue job.

This typically involves updating the JDE job status and performing cleanup operations after a successful extraction and UBL generation. The jobNumber identifies the BIP job, processingType specifies the pipeline step, and baseName is the extracted file's base name.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Extracts data from the JDE BIP Print Queue (F9563110 / F95630 / F95631). extractMode: 'input' (XML from dataOutput), 'output' (files from xmlpOutput), 'both'. outputType filters output by XOFRPOUTYP (XML, PDF, EXCEL, etc.).

Returns the base file name and outputCount for use in subsequent processing.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Extracts XML data for an invoice identified by DOC, DCT, and KCO.

The `source` parameter controls which table and column to read from: `xml` (default) reads the raw source XML from F564230.FETXFT, `ubl` reads the generated UBL 2.1 XML from F564231.UHTXFT. The file is written to the specified outputDir.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Downloads an XML file from a remote SFTP server using the connection credentials configured in the global template (sftpHost, sftpUser, sftpPassword, sftpPort).

The file path is constructed from the report name, version, language, and job number. The downloaded file is saved to the specified output path.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Returns the list of available endpoints for a given api-connector template.

Each endpoint includes its name, HTTP method, URL pattern, and parameter definitions. The connector template must have type=api-connector in its properties. Use this to discover available operations before calling a connector.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Executes a call to a specific endpoint on an api-connector template.

The connector handles authentication, URL construction, and parameter substitution. Parameters are passed as key-value pairs in the request body and substituted into URL placeholders or sent as query/body parameters depending on the endpoint definition. Returns the HTTP status code, response body, and optionally an extracted value.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Probes the named api-connector's authentication (for OAUTH2, fetches a token from the token endpoint) without calling any business endpoint.

Returns the HTTP status of the token call, the token endpoint used, a redacted token preview and a human-readable message. Use this from the Settings test panel to verify credentials before wiring endpoints.

**Access:** settings (feature).

get.description:
Counterpart of /api/connectors for sql-connector templates: returns the queries declared on the named template (name, description, statement type) without exposing credentials.

Use this to discover the available queries before running one.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Runs the named query on the sql-connector with the caller-supplied parameters bound into the statement.

SELECTs return columns plus rows (each cell stringified for transport, so Oracle and Postgres types travel safely); writable statements are only allowed when the connector opts in. Returns the statement type, duration, update count and any error.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Returns validation errors from the validation table (F564236) that have no matching entry in the invoice header table (F564230).

These represent UBL transformation failures where the invoice record could not be created. Supports pagination, full-text search, severity level filtering, and sorting. Use this to monitor and diagnose systemic transformation issues.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Full-text search on DOC, DCT, KCO fields

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Filter by severity: FATAL, ERROR, WARNING, or INFO

post.summary: Send email with optional invoice PDF
post.description:
Sends an email via the SMTP server configured in the global template (smtpHost, smtpPort, smtpUser, etc.).

PDF attachment is resolved in order of priority: (1) If attachmentBase64 is provided, it is decoded and used directly as the PDF attachment. (2) Otherwise, if doc/dct/kco are provided (the (doc, dct, kco) composite key) or ublNumber is provided, the PDF is generated server-side from the UBL XML stored in the database, with optional language parameter for label translation. The email body is sent as plain text. The CC field is optional.

**Access:** invoice.email.

get.description:
Lists files and subdirectories at the given server path.

Supports %APP_HOME% and %PROCESS_HOME% placeholders in the path. Returns an array of entries with name, type (file/directory), size, and modification date. If path is empty or omitted, lists the root of the configured appHome directory.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute server path or path with placeholders (empty = root)

get.description:
Returns the UTF-8 content of a server-side text file at the specified path.

Supports %APP_HOME% and %PROCESS_HOME% placeholders. Intended for reading configuration files, XSL templates, and XML documents. Binary files will be returned as-is but may not display correctly.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute server path to the file

put.description:
Writes or overwrites a server-side text file with the supplied UTF-8 content.

The parent directory must exist. Supports %APP_HOME% and %PROCESS_HOME% placeholders. Use this for editing XSL templates, configuration files, or XML documents in place.

**Access:** settings (feature).

post.description:
Copies a server-side file from source path to destination path.

Both paths support %APP_HOME% and %PROCESS_HOME% placeholders. The destination directory must exist. If the destination file already exists, it is overwritten.

**Access:** settings (feature).

Uploads a file to the template's input directory (dirInput).

The file content is sent as the raw request body (not multipart). The template and filename are specified as query parameters. The dirInput path is resolved from the global template with placeholder substitution. Use this to upload XML files for processing via the /api/run endpoint.

**Access:** settings (feature).

Extracts and installs the built-in XSL framework files (UBL stylesheets, common templates) from the JAR's xsl/ resources into the specified target directory.

This is used during initial setup or when upgrading the XSL framework. Existing files in the target directory with the same names are overwritten.

**Access:** settings (feature).

Searches the French government's entreprise registry API (recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr) for companies matching the given query string.

The query can be a company name, SIREN, SIRET, or any partial match. Returns up to perPage results (configured in the e-directory template, default 10). This is a free public API and does not require authentication. Use this to look up company identifiers for directory checks or invoice addressing.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Look up a SIREN in the public Peppol network
post.description:
Anonymous three-step lookup: the Peppol Directory business card (directory.peppol.eu — participant identifiers, name, registration date; French registrations use ICD 0225), then per participant the SML DNS NAPTR resolution to its SMP host, and the SMP service metadata whose AS4 certificate identifies the service provider (the French 'PA'): subject O= is the provider name, CN= its Peppol seat id.

Each resolution step is best-effort — a participant found in the directory is returned even when the SML/SMP step fails (see its error field). Because a business card is optional, the deterministic French identifiers are also probed in DNS — 0225:SIREN, 0002:SIREN, 0225:<id> for every PPF directory identifier passed in the optional identifiers[] (bare, suffixed SIREN_FGX, SIRET, routed — the French Peppol identifiers are exactly those) and 0009:SIRET for the optional sirets[] (head office first, 25 at most): a participant registered on an SMP without a business card is returned with source=dns and the optional name. SML zone: participant.sml.prod.tech.peppol.org (Peppol SML, 2026), with the legacy EC zone as fallback, through the server's resolver only unless the e-directory setting peppolPublicDns=Y allows 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1 as a fallback when it gives no answer. With the e-directory setting peppolResolveSmp=N the lookup stops after the SML step: smpUrl is filled (its host names the provider), apProvider / apSeat / apEndpoint stay empty — for networks that do not allow HTTPS to the providers' SMP hosts. directoryError is set when the directory was unreachable but the DNS probes still ran. No API key required; needs outbound DNS + HTTPS to the public Peppol infrastructure.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
What the E-Directory page shows, in one call. q is a company name, SIREN or SIRET.

Returns the INSEE companies matching the query (head office and matching establishments; a bare SIREN / SIRET is re-searched by company name so the establishments come back, as the page does), and for each company the PPF directory lines registered for its SIREN through the e-directory connector (directory.configured=false when the connector defines no listing endpoint; directory.error when the lookup failed for that company). peppol=true adds the Peppol participants per company (three network hops each — off by default). Also accepted as POST with body {q, peppol}.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Same result as the GET form, with q and peppol in the JSON body instead of the query string — for callers whose client cannot set query parameters, or when the query holds characters that are awkward in a URL.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Streams an AI assistant response as Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Each event contains a 'data' field with a text token. The stream ends with 'data: [DONE]'. The messages array follows the standard chat format with role (user/assistant/system) and content. The model parameter selects the AI model (default: global.aiModel, else Sonnet 5.5). The optional context object carries what the user is looking at — page, filter, open invoice {doc,dct,kco,status…} — and is given to the model as UI context. The assistant grounds product answers on the documentation indexed from llms-full.txt (search_docs / read_doc_page) and reads this instance's data through read-only tools (invoice dossier, dashboards, server log, integrity checks, settings with secrets masked). Content-Type of the response is text/event-stream.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Returns the JAR's build metadata (version, build date, Git commit) for diagnostics and the About modal.

**Access:** public, no token needed.

post.description:
Compares the live database schema against the bundled DDL — reports missing tables/columns plus type and size mismatches per table.

Used by the migration wizard.

**Access:** settings (feature).

get.description:
Returns the static metadata the DbNomaubl → Columns editor needs to render: ordered table groups, each with its column field/key/default.

Static — never changes per install — so the React tab can fetch it once. The actual override values live in the {@code db-nomaubl-columns} template ({@code config-columns.json}) and are read via the standard /api/config/template endpoint.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Returns the named status-code groups defined in the statuses template — the single source of truth shared by backend SQL filters and frontend dashboard counters, so neither side has to inline its own IN ('9904','9905',…) list.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Returns the column/filter spec that drives a spec-driven list page (invoices, documents, integrationErrors, processingLog, ereporting).

Reads the stored view.<name> property from the db-nomaubl template first, falling back to the bundled default shipped in the JAR — so a fresh install renders without operator configuration; source tells the caller which one won. Saving an edited spec goes through the standard /api/config/template endpoints.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.summary: Column catalog for a list view
get.description:
Returns every column the Java handler can SELECT or filter on for the named view — the Settings editor's '+ Add column' picker reads this to offer columns the current spec doesn't yet include.

Each entry exposes name, labelEn, labelFr and a coarse type (string | number | date). Views without a registered catalog return an error and the editor hides the Add button.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: View name — invoices, documents, integrationErrors, processingLog or ereporting

get.description:
Every text the PDF generator prints (46 keys: document header, parties, lines table, line details, VAT summary, totals, payment) with its default English and French wording.

A PDF template may override any of them per language through its labels block ({ "labels": { "fr": { key: text }, "en": { key: text } } }); blank = default. Edited in the visual builder's Labels panel; the override only applies to documents rendered with that template.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Read-only inventory of every block the PDF template engine knows about, with its label, help text and editable configuration fields.

Drives the visual builder's '+ Add section' picker and the per-card auto-generated form — a new block added in Java shows up here automatically.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.summary: Dashboard overview (all widgets in one call)
get.description:
Single bulk endpoint that returns every dashboard widget at once — daily volume, by-company breakdown, stale invoices, recent lifecycle events, top failing rules, and PA round-trip stats.

Each section swallows its own errors so a single broken sub-query never fails the whole panel.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: excludeReviewed
parameters.description: true = drop reviewed invoices (UHALRTPSD = Y) that sit in an errorTech / errorBusiness status; other statuses keep them. Default false.

get.description:
Single-call feed for the Tech Dashboard: last FATAL/ERROR entries (validation failures and runtime processing log, unioned), 14-day throughput by mode, table row counts, error trend, active sessions (F564252 when auth is on, the in-memory IP tracker otherwise), per-template stats and retry rate.

Sections degrade to empty arrays on error rather than failing the whole call.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Incremental fetch for the live processing-log widget: returns up to 50 of today's runtime events newer than the since timestamp, newest first, plus a now marker the client passes back as the next since.

Bounded to the current day so the query stays on the index.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO timestamp of the newest event already displayed

get.description:
Sanity-checks the running configuration (global paths, db-nomaubl connector, e-invoicing / e-directory / e-reporting templates, license) and returns a flat list of issues with a severity level: error (required setting missing or unusable), warn (non-blocking but worth flagging) or info (diagnostic only).

The IT dashboard surfaces these before a misconfiguration bites at processing time.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

issues.message: Input directory not set — Fetch Input will fail

get.description:
Flat grouped invoice counts and tax-exclusive amounts (sum of UHATXA, BT-109) by activity code (F564230.FEAA10), status, PA reason code and transaction type (B2B / B2G / B2C / B2BINT).

The server returns raw grouped rows; all pivoting, subtotals and percentages are presentation concerns handled client-side. dateBasis selects which date the range filters on: update (UHUPMJ, default), issue (invoice date) or archive (F564230.FEUPMJ). Company and row-level grants apply.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: excludeReviewed
parameters.description: true = drop reviewed invoices (UHALRTPSD = Y) that sit in an errorTech / errorBusiness status; other statuses keep them. Default false.

get.description:
Lists the SQL integrity checks defined in the integrity-reports template (name, description, connector, key columns, SQL).

Each check is a SELECT run against a db connector whose rows are the anomalies to act on — e.g. JDE print jobs never integrated, or accounting records whose amounts differ from the e-invoices.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Executes one configured check read-only (SELECT / WITH only, single statement) against its db connector, capped by the template's maxRows (default 5000) and timeoutSeconds (default 120).

Date placeholders in the SQL are substituted from the optional range: {from} / {to} (yyyy-MM-dd), {fromJde} / {toJde} (JDE julian CYYDDD), {fromDMY} / {toDMY} (dd-MM-yyyy); defaults 1900-01-01 and today. BIP placeholders from the fetch-invoices report list: {bipFilter:REPORTCOL,VERSIONCOL} (report/version predicate), {bipReports} (quoted names for IN), {bipTemplate:REPORTCOL,VERSIONCOL} (CASE giving the document template). Returns the result columns and rows as they come from the database.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Run a check's action on selected rows
post.description:
Executes the follow-up action configured on the check for the selected result rows.

Action fetch-bip integrates the JDE BI Publisher job of each row — the same as the command `fetch-single <template> bip <job> AUTO` — through the fetch-invoices run-batch: jobs[] are the values of the check's job column, templates[] of its template column (else the check's fixed template), hosts[] of its host column (optional, multi-host JDE). Returns the run-batch result (per-file success and logs, summary).

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Returns the column whitelist (name, labels, type) for one queryable dataset so the query builder can offer columns and filters.

Datasets: invoices, documents, lifecycle, validationErrors.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

The data explorer's model (docs/plans/data-explorer.md): one entity per table around the invoice key (invoices, documents, lifecycle, validationErrors, lines, vat, notifications) with its fields — key entity.name, labels, type (string, number, date, datetime), kind (dimension or measure), default aggregate, reference list — and the relations to the hub.

The SQL of a field is the list-view catalog's; the bundled config/model/nomaubl.json (overridable under the environment's config/model) carries labels, measures and relations. Open to the Reports page's readers.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Aggregate: body {entity, rows: [{field, bucket}], measures: [{field, agg}], filters: {key: value}, sort: [{key, dir}], limit}.

Dimensions come from the entity and its related ones (at most one detail entity may provide rows); a detail entity's measure is aggregated per invoice in a sub-query so rows never multiply; a filter on a detail entity becomes an EXISTS. Date dimensions take a bucket (day, week, month, quarter, year), computed from the day-level groups the database returns, so every JDBC dialect works. Aggregates: count, countDistinct, sum, avg, min, max; amounts are returned in real units. Filters use the list-view convention keyed by entity.name (name, name__op, nameFrom, nameTo). Without rows and measures the body {entity, columns: [], page, pageSize} returns detail rows. calculated: [{name, label, labelFr, expr}] adds fields calc.<name> compiled from a small expression language (arithmetic, conditions, ? :, in, is empty, age, days, year, month, round, abs, coalesce) over the fields of the entity and its one-to-one entities — never free SQL. The role's company and row grants scope every statement. debug: true adds the SQL.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
The saved analyses the caller may see (shared ones and the caller's own), one JSON file each under the configuration folder's analyses/ directory: id, name, description, owner, shared, updatedAt and the definition the Explorer page saved (entity, rows, measures, filters, period, view…).

On the first call the former query tool's saved reports are converted into detail analyses.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Body {id?, name, description?, shared?, definition}.

The id is derived from the name when absent; an existing id is replaced (its owner kept). The definition is stored as sent.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

delete.description:
Removes the saved analysis file under the configuration folder's analyses/ directory; the id is the file name.

get.description:
The dashboards the caller may see (shared ones and the caller's own), one JSON file each under the configuration folder's dashboards/ directory: id, name, owner, shared, updatedAt and the definition — a global period preset and the tiles, each a saved analysis id with a width in grid columns (1–4) and a height (s, m, l).

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Body {id?, name, description?, shared?, definition{period, tiles}}.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

delete.description:
Removes the dashboard file under the configuration folder's dashboards/ directory; the analyses of its tiles are kept.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Explorer analysis or dashboard as PDF
post.description:
Body {lang, kind: analysis|dashboard, title, period, sections:[{title, note, chart?:{type: bar|hbar|line|donut, title, labels[], series[{name, values[]}]}, table[[…]], headRows}]}.

get.description:
Free column selection over a whitelisted dataset. columns is a comma-separated list of catalog column names (unknown names are dropped silently; an empty selection is an error).

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: Comma-separated catalog column names to select

get.description:
Returns the saved-reports store (config-reports.json, kept next to the environment config so it can be backed up and promoted between servers on its own). data is {"reports":{}} when nothing has been saved yet.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Stores the request body verbatim into config-reports.json — the server only checks that it is a JSON object and otherwise treats it as opaque; the frontend owns the document shape.

PUT is accepted as an alias for POST.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:

Read-only by design — entering or amending VAT declarations is the accounting system's job; NomaUBL only summarises invoices. **Access:** any signed-in user.

processes.lastLine: ** INFO ** RUN ** START : Processing AUTO — template=r42565, file=26038904_RX_00005

get.summary: Tail of the server log file
get.description:
Reads the end of the server log file — the file the launcher redirected stdout to (resolved through /proc/self/fd/1 on Linux), else global.serverLogFile — and returns its lines newest first, split into severity / module / submodule / message when they follow the ' ** LEVEL ** MODULE ** SUB : msg' form. tailKb (default 512, max 8192) bounds the read; severity (comma list, OTHER = unstructured lines), module and q (text) filter; modules lists the modules seen in the tail. get.description:

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Starts the e-reporting handler in the background (no-op when a run is already in progress) — generates the XML, validates it, persists it, optionally submits to the PA.

Returns at once with {running:true}; poll GET /api/ereporting/generate/progress for the live log and the final summary. {@code start}/{@code end} default to the next-due period for the configured frequency when omitted.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Log lines of the background generation started by POST /api/ereporting/generate, plus running:true while it works. success is false when a line of severity ERROR was emitted (e.g. a report that failed the Flux 10 validation).

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Resend an e-report to the PA
post.description:
Re-submits an existing report's stored XML to the PA, reusing the per-company token configured under {@code e-invoicing-{kco}}.

Updates status + lifecycle the same way the initial submission would.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Cancel + rebuild an e-report for the same period
post.description:
Unflags the report's invoices (so they become selectable again), keeps the row for audit with the 9959 'Annule — regenere' status, then reruns the normal generation for the same company and flux with the original period — a NEW report picks up the unflagged invoices plus any late arrivals.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Returns the period the next run would generate for a company: the frequency of its e-reporting-{kco} template (default e-reporting) unless frequency is given, starting the day after the last report of that company and direction — validation-failed and cancelled reports excluded, as the run does — or the current period when none exists. frequencySource says where the frequency came from, lastPeriodEnd the report it follows (empty when none).

Used by the Generate dialog to pre-fill the period picker.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.description: Company code (required for the last-period lookup)

parameters.name: frequency

get.description:
Returns the current user's notification inbox. Supports unread-only filter and a per-page cap (default 50, max 500).

Lightweight count for the bell-badge query — runs as the authenticated user.

Fires the rule's channels (portal + email + action) once with synthetic invoice data, so the user can verify the wiring without waiting for a real status change.

example.summary: Notified user@example.com via portal+email; action ACK queued

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of every archived document from the archive log (F564230), LEFT JOIN the UBL header (F564231) for status / UBL metadata.

This is the inverse of /api/invoices: it lists ALL documents, whether or not they became a UBL invoice — the UBL-header fields (status, ublNumber, customerName, template…) are null for documents that were never processed. The result columns and filterable fields are spec-driven (list-view 'documents'); any column marked filterable in the spec can be passed as a query parameter keyed by its column name (doc, dct, kco, sourceFile, customerName, statusCode…). Results honour the caller's company / row-level access grants.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: sortBy

parameters.name: sortDir
parameters.description: Sort direction: ASC or DESC (default DESC)

parameters.name: dateBasis
parameters.description: Which date the period filters on: 'update' (FEUPMJ archive date, default) or 'issue' (FEIVD invoice date)

get.description:
Returns the archived source spool XML for the document, read from F564230.FETXFT.

This is the raw JDE spool captured before UBL transformation and is present for every archived document. Access is gated by the caller's company / row grants; an unauthorised or unknown key is reported as missing.

Trips the job's cancellation flag — the job stops at its next loop iteration; rows already processed stay processed. Returns an error for an unknown job id.

get.description:
Every row from the upgrades.db journal in the environment directory, newest first — release id, type, applied timestamp / user / program, one-line summary and the relative report path.

Read-only: triggering an upgrade is a CLI-only operation (./nomaubl.sh upgrade <env>) since a running web server can't stop and restart itself reliably.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

get.summary: Full upgrade report for one run
get.description:
The full JSON report saved by the upgrade orchestrator for one journal row (schema migrations, config additions, XSL merges…), passed through verbatim inside the standard envelope. report is null when the row has no saved report file.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.summary: Fire a daily digest on demand
post.description:
Runs the named daily-digest resource immediately and returns the one-line summary the scheduler would log — useful for verifying the SMTP route and recipient list without waiting for the scheduled hour.

Digest CRUD goes through the standard /api/config/template endpoints; this endpoint only exposes the test trigger.

get.summary: Errors — one list over every store
get.description:
Lists failures with one shape whatever their store: validation findings (F564236), PA rejections and send / import failures (lifecycle events of the errorBusiness and errorTech status groups), processing failures (per-file rows of the runtime log) and job failures (job run rows).

Each row carries when, kind, source (invoice number, file or job), template, company, current status, level, rule, message and resolved. Unresolved (default) hides failures that no longer apply: the invoice left the error statuses, moved on from the event's status, or a later successful END exists for the file or job. Pages are merged across stores newest first; counts gives the total per kind. Company grants of the signed-in user apply to the invoice-linked kinds.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Comma-separated kinds: validation, rejection, failure, processing, job (default all)

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: fr (default) or en, for the status labels

get.summary: Audit report of a period (Markdown or PDF)
get.description:
Generates the audit report of the instance over a period from the NomaUBL tables only (the platform is not queried): scope, executive summary with the previous period and the variation (processed, deposited, approved, refused, rejected, in error, pending, excluded, received, deposited amounts, first-pass validation rate, terminal share, delays creation to deposit and deposit to first buyer status) and findings in words, volumes per month, company, document, transaction type and VAT category, the situation at generation time by status and family, the errors and their handling (findings by rule and source, rejections and refusals by reason, send and import failures, resolved / reviewed / open by age, resends and reprocesses), the lifecycle milestones per month and delays, and consistency checks (platform identifier, archived UBL, stale pending, duplicates, VAT and net totals against the stored lines, invoices awaiting an action without follow-up (to fix and resend, new invoice to issue), optionalSQL integrity checks against JDE).

parameters.name: sections

The file produced by a background audit run, returned once; 404 when the job is unknown, still running or already fetched.

parameters.name: date

parameters.name: sections

get.description:
Lists the configuration items that can be promoted to another instance in this release: document templates with the files they reference (pre-processing and indexation XSL, RTF, UBL XSLT and its PDF companion, custom Schematron) and the PDF template they name, PDF templates, reference and custom lists.

Each item carries its dependencies (files relative to the environment root, other items). Requires the settings feature.

Builds a ZIP with manifest.json (items, kind, checksum, source instance and release, author, date), one JSON fragment per item under items/ and the referenced files under files/ (paths relative to the environment root, so %APP_HOME% / %ENV% placeholders stay valid on the target).

Same response as the preview with applied=true. Requires the settings feature.

**Access:** settings (feature).

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: Comment recorded with the snapshots and the log entry

get.description:
The instances defined in Settings › Promotion targets (instance.N.name / url / username / password): name and URL only, the account never leaves the server. configured=false when the promotion template does not exist yet.

Requires the settings feature.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

post.description:
Builds the package of the given items (as the export does), signs in on the target instance named in target (an instance of Settings › Promotion targets: its URL and account are read on the server) and calls the target's own /api/promotion/preview (apply=false, dry run) or /api/promotion/import (apply=true).

Returns the target's answer with the target URL added. A promotion that applied is one entry of this instance's promotion history; the target records its import. Requires the settings feature.

Kept as one JSON file per entry under the environment's promotions folder. Requires the settings feature.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Requires the settings feature.

Bundled into the JAR at build time (META-INF/xref/dictionary.json) and served verbatim — drives the Data dictionary page.

post.description:
Runs nomaubl.sh demo in the background: deterministic fictitious companies, customers and suppliers, invoices as UBL files, JDE-like spools, text PDFs and received supplier invoices, processed by the real pipelines, then driven through realistic lifecycle paths with dated events, e-reporting envelopes of the completed months and portal notifications.

Body values are strings: invoices (default 300), months (6), seed (2026), sources (ubl,jde,pdf,recv), from (yyyy-MM). Poll GET /api/jobs/{id}: the summary follows the progress and ends with the run's counts. Refused unless global.demoInstance = Y; requires global.updateDB = Y and the environment's framework stylesheets.

**Access:** any signed-in user.

Removes everything the demo created: the invoices of the four demo documents in every table, the e-reporting envelopes of the demo companies, the notification rows of the demo rule, the generated files, inputs, processing trees and mappings, the demo documents and the demo rule. Returns a job id.

**Access:** any signed-in user.
